question: A 12-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and nausea. He first began to have diffuse abdominal pain 15 hours prior to presentation. Since then, the pain has moved to the right lower quadrant. On physical exam he has tenderness to light palpation with rebound tenderness. Lifting his right leg causes severe right lower quadrant pain. Which of the following nerves roots was most likely responsible for the initial diffuse pain felt by this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Initial diffuse abdominal pain" -> "Innervation by visceral afferent fibers" -> "T10 nerve root" -> 80% CHAIN: "Initial diffuse abdominal pain" -> "Visceral pain fibers converge at T10-L1 spinal cord levels" -> "T10 nerve root" -> 75% CHAIN: "Initial diffuse abdominal pain" -> "Referred pain pattern to the right lower quadrant" -> "T10 nerve root" -> 80%
analysis: The initial diffuse abdominal pain felt by the patient is likely due to irritation of the visceral afferent fibers from the midgut structures. The midgut structures receive their sensory innervation from the T10 nerve root.
